scenario_text: A purified enzyme converts a substrate into product in a controlled initial-rate assay while total enzyme, substrate, and a competing small-molecule inhibitor are independently varied. The response is the instantaneous product-formation rate predicted from enzyme–substrate binding, catalytic turnover, and inhibitor occupancy of free enzyme. The algebraic model is obtained by reducing mass-action binding and catalytic balances under a rapid-intermediate approximation, with catalytic constants and binding affinities held fixed across assays.
baseline_mechanisms: Reversible binding of substrate to free enzyme.
Reversible occupancy of the same free-enzyme binding site by a competing inhibitor.
Catalytic conversion of the enzyme–substrate complex into product with product release.
Rapid-intermediate reduction yielding an instantaneous initial-rate response.
baseline_assumptions: Substrate and inhibitor concentrations remain effectively constant during the initial-rate measurement.
The enzyme is conserved among free, substrate-bound, and inhibitor-bound forms.
Only substrate-bound enzyme undergoes productive catalysis, while inhibitor-bound enzyme is catalytically inactive.
Product accumulation, reverse catalysis, and enzyme inactivation are negligible during the measurement.
scientific_constraints: E_tot, S, I, and v must be nonnegative.
The productive catalytic rate cannot exceed the fixed turnover capacity associated with the available total enzyme.
Increasing inhibitor occupancy cannot increase the productive fraction of enzyme under the baseline mechanism.
refinement_agenda: Add substrate inhibition through formation of a nonproductive enzyme–substrate complex at high substrate concentration.
Add cooperative or multimeric substrate binding so that occupancy is no longer described by independent single-site binding.
Add product binding and product inhibition when measurements extend beyond the initial-rate window.
Relax the constant-concentration assumption to model substrate depletion and product accumulation over time.

domain_mechanisms.description: finite enzyme occupancy or catalytic capacity

spec.target_description: Initial product-formation rate per unit assay volume

input_symbols.description: Total enzyme concentration in the assay, in molar units
Competing inhibitor concentration, in molar units

scenario_text: Model the intracellular calcium concentration in a postsynaptic dendritic compartment following a fixed presynaptic spike protocol. Calcium enters through voltage-gated and synaptic calcium channels during prescribed spike-locked events, while intracellular extrusion returns calcium toward its resting level. The scientific target is the instantaneous rate of change of calcium concentration along the resulting neural trajectory. The spike timing and channel activation pattern are fixed background conditions rather than independently sampled inputs.
baseline_mechanisms: Spike-locked calcium influx through neuronal membrane channels
First-order intracellular calcium extrusion and relaxation toward rest
baseline_assumptions: The dendritic compartment is well mixed, so calcium has one spatially uniform dynamic concentration
The presynaptic spike timing and channel activation waveform are fixed throughout each trajectory
Calcium buffering is absorbed into effective influx and extrusion parameters
Extrusion strength is proportional to the elevation above the resting calcium level
scientific_constraints: Intracellular calcium concentration must remain non-negative
Calcium influx is non-negative during each prescribed activation event
With finite influx and positive extrusion, concentration remains bounded
refinement_agenda: Add a separate dynamic buffer or bound-calcium state
Replace linear extrusion with a saturating calcium-clearance mechanism
Add calcium-dependent channel inactivation or feedback on influx
Change the fixed spike protocol assumption to allow variable presynaptic timing or burst structure

domain_mechanisms.description: finite capacity, resource limitation, or saturation

spec.target_description: Instantaneous rate of change of postsynaptic intracellular calcium concentration

required_dynamic_states.description: Postsynaptic intracellular calcium concentration in a dendritic compartment

expected_behaviors: Calcium concentration rises during prescribed calcium-permeable channel activation events
Calcium concentration relaxes toward a low resting level between activation events
The response remains bounded over the modeled interval
Larger calcium influx produces a larger transient increase in concentration
forbidden_behaviors: Unbounded calcium accumulation under a finite fixed spike protocol
Spontaneous oscillations without changes in the prescribed neural drive
Dependence on independently sampled input coordinates

scenario_text: A directly transmitted infection spreads through a closed, homogeneously mixing population containing susceptible, infectious, and recovered individuals. Infectious individuals generate new infections through contact with susceptible people, while infectious individuals leave the infectious state through recovery. The benchmark targets the instantaneous change in the infectious population over a 180-day outbreak trajectory. Demographic turnover, latent infection, reinfection, and intervention changes are treated as absent in the baseline model.
baseline_mechanisms: Contact-mediated transmission from infectious to susceptible individuals.
Removal of infectious individuals through recovery.
Transfer of susceptible individuals into the infectious class upon successful transmission.
Transfer of infectious individuals into the recovered class after recovery.
baseline_assumptions: The population is closed during the modeled interval, with no births, deaths, or migration.
Individuals mix homogeneously and have equal infectious contact opportunities.
Infection and recovery rates are constant over time.
Recovered individuals remain immune and cannot return to the susceptible class during the modeled interval.
scientific_constraints: All three population states must remain nonnegative.
The sum of susceptible, infectious, and recovered individuals is conserved.
Each population state cannot exceed the conserved total population.
Transmission cannot decrease the susceptible population or increase the recovered population directly.
refinement_agenda: Add demographic entry and exit to represent births, deaths, and migration.
Introduce a latent, noninfectious stage to represent delayed onset of infectiousness.
Add waning immunity and return of recovered individuals to susceptibility.
Allow time-varying contact rates or intervention-mediated reductions in transmission.
Add disease-induced mortality as a separate removal pathway from the infectious class.

domain_mechanisms.description: contact or transmission response changes with prevalence or density
risk response changes contact or control behavior
finite immunity duration or recovery transition

spec.target_description: Instantaneous rate of change of the infectious population

required_dynamic_states.description: Number of recovered and immune individuals

scenario_text: Track the frequency of a favored allele in a large, randomly mating population across generations, assuming that its relative reproductive success advantage remains constant. The allele frequency changes through deterministic viability and reproductive selection, with no mutation, migration, or random sampling effects. The benchmark should learn the time-dependent rate of allele-frequency change from the current allele frequency and a fixed positive selection intensity. The resulting trajectory should approach fixation without crossing the valid frequency bounds.
baseline_mechanisms: Deterministic directional selection favoring one allele
Frequency dependence of selection response caused by the requirement that both allelic types be present for replacement to occur
baseline_assumptions: The population is sufficiently large that random sampling effects are negligible.
Mating is random and generations are represented by a continuous-time approximation.
The selective advantage is constant across time and independent of population density or environmental state.
There are only two allelic alternatives at the locus, with allele frequencies summing to one implicitly.
scientific_constraints: Allele frequency must remain in the closed interval from zero to one.
The favored allele frequency is nondecreasing under the specified positive selection regime.
The complementary allele frequency is nonnegative and decreases as the favored allele rises.
refinement_agenda: add_term: recurrent mutation between the two alleles, allowing loss and reintroduction of the favored allele
add_term: migration from a source population with a different allele frequency
change_assumption: allow selection intensity to vary with time or environmental conditions
change_assumption: include random genetic drift in a finite population formulation

domain_mechanisms.description: finite capacity, resource limitation, or saturation

spec.target_description: Instantaneous rate of change of the favored allele frequency

required_dynamic_states.description: Frequency of the favored allele in the population

expected_behaviors: The allele frequency remains between zero and one throughout the trajectory.
For a positive fixed selective advantage, the allele frequency increases monotonically from its initial value.
The rate of change is small when the allele is rare or nearly fixed and largest at intermediate frequency.
The trajectory approaches fixation asymptotically rather than overshooting it.
forbidden_behaviors: The allele frequency may not become negative or exceed one.
The trajectory must not oscillate or reverse direction under constant positive selection.
The baseline trajectory must not include random genetic drift, mutation-driven recurrence, migration, or recombination-dependent changes.
The model must not create or destroy population-frequency mass outside the two-allele frequency representation.
